description: Serial transmitter: on tx_start pulse, sends start bit, 8 data bits LSB-first, stop bit. tx_busy indicates active transmission. bit_clk assumed to be exactly 1 bit period.
solution:
module uart_tx (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire tx_start,
    input wire [7:0] tx_data,
    output reg tx,
    output reg tx_busy
);
    reg [3:0] state;
    reg [7:0] shift;
    always @(posedge clk)
        if (rst) begin
            tx<=1'b1; tx_busy<=1'b0; state<=4'd0;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                4'd0: begin
                    tx <= 1'b1; tx_busy <= 1'b0;
                    if (tx_start) begin
                        shift <= tx_data;
                        tx_busy <= 1'b1;
                        state <= 4'd1;
                    end
                end
                4'd1: begin tx <= 1'b0; state <= 4'd2; end // start
                4'd2: begin tx <= shift[0]; shift <= {1'b0, shift[7:1]}; state <= 4'd3; end
                4'd3: begin tx <= shift[0]; shift <= {1'b0, shift[7:1]}; state <= 4'd4; end
                4'd4: begin tx <= shift[0]; shift <= {1'b0, shift[7:1]}; state <= 4'd5; end
                4'd5: begin tx <= shift[0]; shift <= {1'b0, shift[7:1]}; state <= 4'd6; end
                4'd6: begin tx <= shift[0]; shift <= {1'b0, shift[7:1]}; state <= 4'd7; end
                4'd7: begin tx <= shift[0]; shift <= {1'b0, shift[7:1]}; state <= 4'd8; end
                4'd8: begin tx <= shift[0]; shift <= {1'b0, shift[7:1]}; state <= 4'd9; end
                4'd9: begin tx <= shift[0]; state <= 4'd10; end
                4'd10: begin tx <= 1'b1; state <= 4'd11; end // stop
                default: begin tx <= 1'b1; tx_busy <= 1'b0; state <= 4'd0; end
            endcase
        end
endmodule

title: Interview: 4-bit LFSR With Maximum Sequence
description: Interview classic: design a 4-bit LFSR that cycles through 15 states (all except all-zeros) before repeating. The standard taps are bits 4 and 3 (q[3] XOR q[2]), and the shift direction is right. Reset loads 4'hF. Verify the sequence has period 15 (excluding zero).
hint: Feedback = q[3] XOR q[2]. Shift left with feedback in LSB. Seed with non-zero 4'hF.

title: Interview: BCD Counter for a Digital Clock
description: Interview question: design the seconds counter of a digital clock. It counts 00..59 in BCD and rolls over. Provide a 1 Hz clock enable input (tick=1 for one cycle every second). Output tens[3:0] and units[3:0]. Synchronous reset to 00. This is the standard 'design a counter' interview block.
solution:
module bcd_seconds (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire tick,
    output reg [3:0] tens,
    output reg [3:0] units
);
    always @(posedge clk)
        if (rst) begin tens<=0; units<=0; end
        else if (tick) begin
            if (tens==4'd5 && units==4'd9) begin tens<=0; units<=0; end
            else if (units==4'd9) begin units<=0; tens<=tens+4'd1; end
            else units<=units+4'd1;
        end
endmodule
hint: Nested BCD counters. Increment units; on units=9 reset units, increment tens; on tens=5 & units=9 rollover.

title: Interview: Byte Swap Without Concatenation
description: Given a 16-bit value, swap its two bytes. The catch: the interviewer says 'you may not use concatenation'. Use shifts and masks only.
hint: Mask each byte, shift in opposite directions, OR them together.

title: Interview: Counter With Programmable Terminal Count
description: Interview question: design an 8-bit up counter with a programmable terminal count. Input reload_val[7:0]. When the counter reaches reload_val, it rolls to 0 and asserts wrap=1 for one cycle. Reset clears to 0. The interviewer expects careful handling of the wrap pulse.
hint: Compare to reload_val; on match reset to 0 and pulse wrap.

title: Interview: Debounce a Button in RTL
description: Interview classic: given a noisy button input (btn) and a 1 kHz clock, produce a clean debounced signal (clean_btn) that only changes after the input has been stable for 20 ms (20 clock cycles for this exercise). Reset clears the counter. The output should not glitch on short spikes.
hint: Count consecutive mismatches; when threshold reached, update output and reset counter.

title: Interview: Find the Maximum Value in a Stream
description: Interview question: values arrive one per clock (in_valid=1). Output the running maximum so far. When last=1, latch the final maximum on max_final and assert done=1. Reset clears the maximum. This is a classic streaming data-path question.
template:
module max_stream (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire in_valid,
    input wire last,
    input wire [7:0] data,
    output reg [7:0] running_max,
    output reg [7:0] max_final,
    output reg done
);
    // Running max, latch at last
endmodule
solution:
module max_stream (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire in_valid,
    input wire last,
    input wire [7:0] data,
    output reg [7:0] running_max,
    output reg [7:0] max_final,
    output reg done
);
    always @(posedge clk)
        if (rst) begin running_max<=0; max_final<=0; done<=0; end
        else begin
            done <= 0;
            if (in_valid) begin
                if (data > running_max) running_max <= data;
                if (last) begin
                    max_final <= (data > running_max) ? data : running_max;
                    done <= 1;
                end
            end
        end
endmodule
hint: Compare-and-update. On last, output max(data, running_max) and pulse done.

title: Interview: Find the Position of the First '1' Bit
description: Interview question: given an 8-bit input, output the index (0-7) of the lowest-order 1 bit, or 0xFF if no bit is set. This is a priority encoder variant. Output is 4 bits (3 for index, 1 for valid flag would also be acceptable, but here we pack it as 4-bit pos where 0..7 are valid and 4'hF means none).
hint: Priority encoder, lowest-index first. Return 4'hF for no-bit set.

title: Interview: Measure a Pulse Width
description: Interview question: given an input signal in, measure the width (in clock cycles) of the HIGH pulse. When in goes high, start counting; when it goes low, latch the count into width_out and pulse done=1. Reset clears. This is a classic timing measurement block.
hint: Detect rising edge (start count), increment while high, latch at falling edge.

title: Interview: Population Count of a 16-bit Word
description: Given a 16-bit input, count the number of 1 bits. Output a 5-bit count (0..16). The interviewer may ask you to do this without a loop, using a tree of adders. Implement with combinational logic.
hint: Sum the bits. A for-loop over 16 bits synthesizes into a tree of adders.

title: Interview: Streaming Odd-Parity Checker
description: Bits arrive MSB-first. After every 8 bits, output odd_parity_ok=1 if the received 8-bit byte (plus the 9th parity bit — ignore this simplification) has an odd number of 1s. Actually simpler: after every 8 valid data bits, assert parity_ok=1 if the count of 1s is odd. Output pulse one cycle after the 8th bit. This is the standard 'parity checker' interview question.
hint: Maintain a running XOR (parity). Every 8 bits, output the parity (of all 8 bits including the last one), then reset.

title: Interview: Swap Two 8-bit Values in Hardware
description: Given two 8-bit registers a and b (not inputs, but internal registers), swap their contents on a start pulse, using no third register. Output new_a and new_b. The interviewer wants to see that you know the XOR swap trick, or that you can simply assign both in the same clock edge using non-blocking assignment in an always_ff-style block. Implement the cleanest solution (non-blocking assignment) — the XOR trick is a C trick, not needed in RTL. But be prepared to explain both.
template:
module swap8 (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire start,
    input wire [7:0] a_in,
    input wire [7:0] b_in,
    output reg [7:0] a_out,
    output reg [7:0] b_out
);
    // Swap on start
endmodule
solution:
module swap8 (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire start,
    input wire [7:0] a_in,
    input wire [7:0] b_in,
    output reg [7:0] a_out,
    output reg [7:0] b_out
);
    always @(posedge clk)
        if (rst) begin a_out <= 0; b_out <= 0; end
        else if (start) begin a_out <= b_in; b_out <= a_in; end
endmodule
hint: Non-blocking assignment makes the swap free — both registers update simultaneously from the old values.
constraints: No temp register in the module

title: Interview: 2-Cycle Pipelined Multiplier
description: Interview question: design an 8x8 multiplier that produces a result in exactly 2 cycles. Inputs: a, b (8 bits each), valid_in. On the next cycle, valid_mid is asserted with the partial results; on the cycle after that, valid_out is asserted with the product. This tests pipelining and handshake design.
template:
module mult2cycle (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire valid_in,
    input wire [7:0] a,
    input wire [7:0] b,
    output reg valid_out,
    output reg [15:0] product
);
    // 2-cycle latency
endmodule
hint: Two-stage pipeline: stage 1 registers valid_in and the product; stage 2 registers valid_stage1 and product_stage1 to output.

title: Interview: Carry-Save Adder for Three Numbers
description: Google-style interview: design a circuit that adds THREE 8-bit unsigned numbers and produces a 9-bit sum, using carry-save technique (one level of 3:2 compressors + one adder), not just a chain of two adders. Though the result is the same, the interviewer wants to see the carry-save structure.
hint: 3:2 compressor produces partial sum and partial carry vectors. Add the two with a single adder (carry shifted left by 1).
constraints: Only one adder at the end

title: Interview: Combine Two Rising Edges Into One Pulse
description: Two inputs a and b each produce rising edges. Design a circuit that produces a single-cycle pulse on the output whenever EITHER a OR b has a rising edge, but not when both occur on the same clock. In other words, if both rise simultaneously, treat it as one event. This is a classic 'event coalescing' interview problem.
hint: Detect rising edges on a and b separately, OR the two pulses. If both rise at the same time, the OR is still one pulse.

title: Interview: Cross-Clock-Domain Pulse Synchronizer
description: Interview classic. A 1-cycle pulse arrives in clock domain A (src_clk). It must be delivered as a 1-cycle pulse in clock domain B (dst_clk). The classic solution: toggle a bit in the source domain on each incoming pulse, sync the toggle through 2 FFs in the destination, and detect the edge in the destination. This problem asks for that exact circuit.
hint: Toggle a bit in src domain, pass through 2 FFs in dst domain, then edge-detect by XORing the two delayed versions.
constraints: Pulse must not duplicate or drop

title: Interview: Divide-by-3 Clock with Exact 50% Duty Cycle
description: Classic interview question. Design a clock divider that takes an input clock and produces an output clock with 1/3 the frequency AND exactly 50% duty cycle. A simple mod-3 counter cannot do this because 3 is odd (you can't split an odd period into two equal halves using a single counter). The trick: use a counter that counts on BOTH edges of the input clock (or two counters: one on posedge, one on negedge) and combine them. Output must be 50% duty for any odd divide ratio in this specific case (divide by 3).
hint: Use two mod-3 counters, one clocked on posedge and one on negedge. Each toggles at half the rate. OR the two toggles to get a 50% duty output.
constraints: Only use clk (no separate negedge clock)

title: Interview: Find the Missing Number in a Stream
description: Interview puzzle: numbers 1..N arrive one per clock (in_valid=1). Exactly one number is missing. Find it. The trick: XOR all arriving numbers with a counter that runs 1..N. The result is the missing number. The stream ends when last=1 (N numbers have arrived, but one is missing so actually N-1 arrived). Assume the stream provides N-1 numbers, and the expected range is 1..N.
hint: XOR the arriving numbers together; also XOR the expected range. The XOR of both is the missing number. Or keep XORing the arriving numbers into acc, and XOR acc with a counter's value at the end.

title: Interview: FSM Detecting Binary Input Divisible by 3
description: Interview classic (Google, Facebook): given a stream of binary bits (MSB first) representing an unsigned integer, output div3=1 when the accumulated number is divisible by 3. There are 3 states, tracking the remainder mod 3. On each bit: new_rem = (old_rem * 2 + bit) % 3.
hint: Three states for remainder 0,1,2. Next state = (2*rem + bit) mod 3.

title: Interview: Glitch-Free Clock Mux
description: Interview classic: given two clocks clk0 and clk1, and a select signal sel, design a glitch-free clock mux. Naive `sel ? clk1 : clk0` glitches when sel changes while the active clock is high. Correct design: register sel in each clock domain, cross-couple to gate each clock, and OR the results. Output must not produce glitches when sel changes.
hint: Each clock has a gating FF that only asserts when its own clock is inactive and the other gating FF is deasserted. OR the gated clocks.

title: Interview: Round-Robin Arbiter for 4 Requesters
description: Interview classic (Qualcomm, NVIDIA): 4 requesters compete for one resource. Fair arbitration (round robin): the last granted requester has lowest priority next time. Output is a one-hot grant. If no requests, grant=0. Reset resets the pointer to 0.
hint: Start scanning from ptr; grant the first requester found. Update ptr to just after the granted index.

title: Interview: Safe Reset Deassertion
description: Classic interview question: design a block that takes an asynchronous reset input rst_n_async and produces a synchronous reset output rst_n_sync that deasserts synchronously to the clock, but asserts asynchronously. This is standard practice to avoid reset removal violations. The output should assert as soon as the async reset asserts (async assert), but deassert cleanly on a clock edge.
hint: Two FFs in series: each clock loads 1 from the previous stage or from a constant 1; the async reset forces both to 0. Output is the second FF.

title: Interview: Stuck-at Fault Detection
description: Interview question for test engineers and DFT: given a stream of bytes, detect if any bit appears to be 'stuck at' a constant value over 100 consecutive samples. In other words, for each bit position, if the bit has been the same (all 0 or all 1) for 100 samples, raise a stuck flag for that bit. Output stuck[7:0]. This is a simplified BIST checker.
hint: Per-bit counters: one for consecutive 0s, one for consecutive 1s. Cap at 100 and set stuck when reached. Reset the other counter on transition.

title: 4-sample Moving Average (hint version)
description: A guided version of the 4-sample moving average. Fill in the else-branch to correctly compute the average and out_valid. The scaffolding is provided; you must complete the DUT logic.
hint: When cnt reaches 3, the window is full. Output next_sum >> 2 and assert out_valid. Otherwise keep counting.

title: XOR-8 Hash over byte stream
description: Compute an 8-bit hash by XORing all incoming bytes. on in_valid, hash ^= in_byte. On last, output hash and assert done.
template:
module xor8_hash (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire in_valid,
    input wire last,
    input wire [7:0] in_byte,
    output reg [7:0] hash,
    output reg done
);
    // XOR hash
endmodule
hint: Simple XOR accumulator. Remember to include the final byte in the output.

title: 4-sample Moving Average
description: Compute a 4-sample moving average of an 8-bit unsigned input stream. Output the average (8 bits) every cycle after the first 4 samples. Use a running sum so no division is needed at run time.
hint: Maintain a rolling sum: add new, subtract the oldest. Use shift to divide by 4. Gate the output until the buffer is full.

title: 4-sample Moving Average (buggy reference)
description: Reference (intentionally buggy) moving average. The bug: the window is updated but the output is computed from the stale accumulator on the first few samples. Fix it so the average is correct from the first full window.
hint: The buggy version uses the old sum for the first valid output and starts one sample too early. Correct by using next_sum and starting at cnt==3.

title: 4-sample Moving Average (efficient)
description: Efficient version of the 4-sample moving average that avoids the subtraction of the oldest sample until the ring is full, using a circular buffer and an extra 'first-cycle' mask.
hint: Ring buffer indexed by a 2-bit pointer. Subtract the value being overwritten, add the new value. Output when cnt==3.
constraints: One subtract + one add per cycle

title: 4-sample Moving Average (fixed)
description: Compute a 4-sample moving average of an 8-bit unsigned input stream. Output the average (8 bits) every cycle after the first 4 samples. Use a running sum so no division is needed at run time.
hint: Use a single update: next_sum = sum - oldest + newest. Take next_sum >> 2 for the average. Start outputting when cnt reaches 3.

title: Add Overflow Detector
description: Detect signed overflow when adding two N-bit two's complement numbers. Overflow occurs when two positives produce a negative, or two negatives produce a positive. Output 1 if signed overflow occurred. Also produce the sum.
hint: Sign-extend both operands by 1 bit, add them, then XOR the two top result bits (sign out vs. carry).
constraints: Signed overflow rule via sign extension

title: Base64 Character Decoder
description: Decode a single Base64 character into a 6-bit value. Mapping: 'A'-'Z' -> 0..25, 'a'-'z' -> 26..51, '0'-'9' -> 52..61, '+' -> 62, '/' -> 63. '=' (padding) produces valid=0. This is a combinational decode step.
hint: Range comparisons with ASCII constants. Use ranges, not 64-case ladders.

title: Signed Absolute Difference
description: Compute |a - b| for two signed 8-bit inputs and output the unsigned result along with the sign of a-b (1 if a>=b).
hint: Widen the subtraction result to 9 bits signed. If the sign bit is 1, negate. Compare sign for the flag.

title: Streaming ASCII strlen
description: Compute the length of a string streamed one character per clock. A byte equal to 0x00 (NUL) terminates; when terminator is seen, done=1 and len holds the count of non-NUL characters.
hint: Increment a counter on each non-NUL valid char; on NUL, output the counter and assert done.

title: ASCII String to Integer (atoi) in RTL
description: Convert an 8-bit ASCII decimal string '0'-'9' presented one character per clock into a running integer value. Maintain acc = acc*10 + (char-'0'). Skip non-digit characters (accumulate only digits). Reset clears the accumulator. Data-valid input indicates the current byte is a valid character; last indicates end of string.
template:
module ascii_atoi (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire data_valid,
    input wire last,
    input wire [7:0] char_in,
    output reg [31:0] value,
    output reg done
);
    // Streaming ASCII-to-integer
endmodule
hint: Multiply-and-add accumulator. On last, push the final computed value to the output and assert done.

title: CAN Bit Stuffer (insert after 5 same bits)
description: Implement a CAN-style bit stuffer: after 5 consecutive identical bits (all 0 or all 1), insert an opposite bit into the output stream. Output stream is 2x speed: for every input bit, optionally emit a stuffed bit in the next cycle. Simplify: one output bit per clock, but the stuffer can assert out_valid twice per input bit (once for data, once for stuff).
hint: Track run length of current value. When it hits 5, set a need_stuff flag; on next cycle emit ~last_bit and reset the run count.
constraints: Insert opposite bit after 5 same bits

title: I2C Start/Stop Condition Detector
description: Given synchronized SDA and SCL inputs, detect I2C Start (SDA falls while SCL is high) and Stop (SDA rises while SCL is high) conditions. Output start_pulse and stop_pulse one-cycle each.
hint: Register both SDA and SCL. Detect edges on SDA only when SCL is high.

title: Integer to ASCII Decimal (fixed width)
description: Convert an 8-bit unsigned integer (0-255) to a 3-digit ASCII string streamed one digit per clock, MSD first. Output valid on each digit. This models a common embedded conversion.
hint: Precompute three digits using division/modulo (synthesizable for constants). Stream them out using a small counter.

title: Internet Checksum (16-bit ones' complement)
description: Compute the Internet checksum over a stream of 16-bit words. Accumulate with end-around carry; complement the final sum. Input words arrive one per clock with in_valid; last signals the final word. This models the IP/TCP checksum computation.
template:
module inet_checksum (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire in_valid,
    input wire last,
    input wire [15:0] word,
    output reg [15:0] checksum,
    output reg done
);
    // 16-bit ones' complement sum, then complement
endmodule
hint: Add each word into a 32-bit acc; fold the top 16 bits into the low half to implement end-around carry. On last, complement the resulting 16-bit sum.

title: Run-Length Encoder (streaming)
description: Streaming RLE: input bytes arrive one per clock with in_valid. Emit (count, value) pairs when the run ends or on the last byte. Count saturates at 255. Emit count and value on consecutive clock cycles.
template:
module rle_encoder (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire in_valid,
    input wire last,
    input wire [7:0] in_byte,
    output reg out_valid,
    output reg [7:0] out_byte
);
    // Emit pairs: count, value
endmodule
hint: Store previous value and run count. When in_byte differs from prev (or last=1), latch count/value into pending and use a 3-state sequencer to emit count then value on consecutive cycles.

examples.input: AA AA AA BB CC CC DD

title: SPI Flash Busy Polling Logic
description: Model the higher-level logic that polls a SPI flash status register until the WIP (write in progress) bit clears. Assert start_poll to begin; the DUT issues read_status pulses; when status returns with WIP=0, assert done.
hint: Simple two-state logic: idle + polling. Emit read_status pulses each cycle while WIP=1; assert done and return to idle when WIP=0.

title: Streaming memcpy-like block copier
description: Model a simple memcpy in RTL: read from a source stream and write to a destination stream. On start, copy LEN bytes from input to output, one per clock. Done asserts on last byte. This models a small DMA-like engine.
template:
module stream_memcpy (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire start,
    input wire [15:0] len,
    input wire in_valid,
    input wire [7:0] in_data,
    output reg out_valid,
    output reg [7:0] out_data,
    output reg done
);
    // Copy 'len' bytes stream-to-stream
endmodule
hint: Single counter running from 0 to len-1. Assert out_valid on each in_valid; assert done when the last byte is passed through.

title: UART Loopback with FIFO
description: Receive a UART byte (assume 1 start, 8 data, 1 stop), push it into a small FIFO, then pop and transmit it back. This models an echo server. Simplify: the testbench drives byte-level in/out rather than bit-level. The DUT handles a byte-in / byte-out FIFO loopback.
hint: Simple FIFO with 5-bit pointers (extra bit for full/empty). Push on rx_valid; pop when not empty.

title: Story: Full Coffee Vending Machine Logic
description: A coffee vending machine has four drinks: espresso (E), cappuccino (C), latte (L), and hot water (W). Prices: E=30c, C=50c, L=60c, W=10c. The user selects one drink with select[1:0] and inserts coins (5c, 10c). The machine outputs the price (combinational) for the selected drink, so a display can show it. If no drink is selected (select=2'b11 for none), the price display is 0 and a 'select' light comes on. This part is combinational.
hint: Simple case statement mapping select to price.

title: Story: Gym Membership Eligibility Logic
description: A gym has an eligibility checker. A person is eligible to enter when: (a) their membership is active (active=1), AND (b) they are either a VIP (vip=1), OR they are within the allowed hours (allowed_hours=1). Additionally, they must not be banned (banned=0). Also, if the gym is full (full=1), nobody can enter except VIPs. Output can_enter=1 if allowed. This is combinational — the turnstile checks instantly.
hint: Read the story and translate the boolean sentence directly into a single assign.

examples.input: active, non-vip, allowed, not banned, not full

title: Story: Smart Home Light Control (Combinational)
description: A smart light turns on based on several inputs: motion=1 (somebody moved), dark=1 (it's dark), override_on=1 (manual switch on), override_off=1 (manual switch off), schedule=1 (it's inside the schedule window). Rules: manual override always wins (override_off forces off, override_on forces on). Otherwise, on if (motion AND dark) OR schedule. This is combinational — the light responds instantly. Write the boolean.
solution:
module smart_light_combo (
    input wire motion,
    input wire dark,
    input wire override_on,
    input wire override_off,
    input wire schedule,
    output wire on
);
    assign on = override_off ? 1'b0 :
                override_on  ? 1'b1 :
                ((motion & dark) | schedule);
endmodule
hint: Nested conditional assign with the priority order given.

title: Story: The 4-Device Bus Arbiter
description: Four devices (A, B, C, D) want to use a shared bus. Their requests arrive on req[3:0], where A is highest priority and D is lowest. The arbiter grants one device at a time via grant[3:0] (one-hot). The arbiter is combinational — the grant responds instantly to requests. If no request, grant=0. Design the priority encoder.
hint: Classic fixed priority encoder.

title: Story: The Airbag Deployment Logic
description: Airbag deployment logic must be robust. Inputs: crash_sensor=1 (impact detected), speed_over_20=1 (vehicle speed above 20 km/h), seat_occupied=1 (someone in the seat). To deploy the airbag, we need crash_sensor AND speed_over_20 AND seat_occupied. However, a defeat switch (child_seat=1) prevents deployment on the passenger side. Also, if the airbag was already deployed (already_fired=1), do not fire again. The output fire=1 pulse. Reset clears already_fired.
hint: Simple AND of conditions with two negations.

title: Story: The Elevator Floor Display Decoder
description: A 12-floor building has an elevator. The cabin has a 4-bit floor register (0..11). A panel of LEDs displays which floor is currently selected. Each floor also has a 'this floor' indicator LED. You need a combinational block that takes the 4-bit floor number and outputs a 12-bit one-hot signal (one LED per floor) for the LED panel, plus an error flag if the floor number is invalid (12..15). No clocks, purely combinational.
hint: Decoder plus range check. Shift 1 left by floor for the one-hot output.

title: Story: The Insurance Premium Calculator
description: An insurance company computes a risk premium from three boolean inputs: young (age<25), smoker, and accident (had an accident last year). The premium level is encoded as 2 bits: 00 = low (no factors), 01 = medium (one factor), 10 = high (two factors), 11 = very high (three factors). Write the combinational logic as a popcount.
hint: Simple sum of three 1-bit signals.

title: Story: The Smart Fridge That Tracks Milk
description: A smart fridge tracks milk bottles. There are three input sensors: put_in=1 pulse when a bottle is added, take_out=1 pulse when a bottle is removed, and spoils=1 pulse when the fridge detects a spoiled bottle. The count must never go negative (a take_out with 0 bottles is ignored). The fridge also warns low=1 when count <= 1. Output count[3:0] (0..15). This is a small saturating counter.
template:
module fridge_milk (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire put_in,
    input wire take_out,
    input wire spoils,
    output reg [3:0] count,
    output wire low
);
    // up/down with floor at 0, cap at 15
endmodule
hint: Standard saturating up/down counter with clamp at 0 and 15.

title: Story: Warehouse Conveyor Package Counter
description: A factory conveyor belt counts packages. A photo-sensor produces a pulse (pkg=1) whenever a package passes. The counter must count up to 65535 and then stop counting (not wrap). The output total[15:0] is the running count. A reset switch (rst) clears the count. This is a saturating counter.
hint: Add a compare against 0xFFFF to prevent wrap.

title: Story: ABS Sensor Pulse Counter
description: You are writing the digital part of an Anti-lock Braking System (ABS). A wheel-speed sensor emits a pulse (sensor_pulse=1) each time a wheel tooth passes. The DUT counts pulses over a fixed window of 100 clocks, then outputs pulses_count and a valid_window pulse. A very low count (<= 2) indicates the wheel is locked (locked=1). A very high count (>= 90) indicates the wheel is spinning too fast (spin=1). Otherwise the wheel is normal. Reset clears counters.
template:
module abs_monitor (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire sensor_pulse,
    output reg [7:0] pulses_count,
    output reg valid_window,
    output reg locked,
    output reg spin
);
    // 100-cycle windows
endmodule
hint: Two counters: pulse count and window count. Latch outputs and reset both counters at the window boundary.

title: Story: Pedestrian Crossing Timer
description: A pedestrian crossing has a countdown timer displayed as a 2-digit BCD number. When the walk button is pressed (start), the timer loads 30 (BCD 3,0) and counts down every clock. When it hits 0, it stops and outputs done=1 for one cycle, then waits. Pressing start again restarts. Reset clears to 0 and idle state. Output units[3:0] and tens[3:0] in BCD.
solution:
module ped_timer (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire start,
    output reg [3:0] units,
    output reg [3:0] tens,
    output reg done
);
    reg running;
    always @(posedge clk)
        if (rst) begin units<=0; tens<=0; done<=0; running<=0; end
        else begin
            done <= 0;
            if (start) begin tens<=4'd3; units<=4'd0; running<=1; end
            else if (running) begin
                if (units==4'd0 && tens==4'd0) begin done<=1; running<=0; end
                else if (units==4'd0) begin units<=4'd9; tens<=tens-4'd1; end
                else units <= units - 4'd1;
            end
        end
endmodule
hint: BCD countdown: when units=0 and tens>0, set units=9 and decrement tens. When both 0, done.

title: Story: The 3-Digit Combination Lock
description: A safe has a 3-digit combination. Each digit is 0-3 (2 bits). The user enters digits one at a time with enter=1 pulse and the digit value digit[1:0]. The correct combination is 1, 2, 3. If the user enters any wrong digit, the lock resets and locks out (locked_out=1) permanently until rst. If the correct three digits are entered, unlock=1 and the counter resets to expect the next sequence. Design the FSM.
solution:
module combo_lock (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire enter,
    input wire [1:0] digit,
    output reg unlock,
    output reg locked_out
);
    reg [1:0] st; // 0=expect 1, 1=expect 2, 2=expect 3, 3=locked
    always @(posedge clk)
        if (rst) begin st<=0; unlock<=0; locked_out<=0; end
        else begin
            unlock <= 0;
            case (st)
                2'd0: if (enter) st <= (digit==2'd1) ? 2'd1 : 2'd3;
                2'd1: if (enter) st <= (digit==2'd2) ? 2'd2 : 2'd3;
                2'd2: if (enter) begin
                        if (digit==2'd3) begin unlock<=1; st<=0; end
                        else st<=2'd3;
                      end
                2'd3: locked_out <= 1;
            endcase
        end
endmodule
hint: FSM with 4 states: expect 1, expect 2, expect 3, locked. Any wrong digit jumps to locked.

title: Story: The ATM That Chooses Which Bills to Give
description: You are designing the bill-dispensing logic of an ATM. The customer requests an amount (amount[15:0] in dollars). The ATM must dispense using the fewest bills. Available: $100, $50, $20. If the amount cannot be made (e.g., $30, because 20+10 has no 10), the ATM must output error=1 and dispense nothing. Otherwise, output n100, n50, n20 (number of each bill) and ready=1. This is purely combinational — the customer presses withdraw and the amounts appear.
hint: Greedy fails for some amounts (e.g., 30 = 20+10 impossible). Amount must be a multiple of 10. Try 50s first, but fall back to fewer 50s when the remainder isn't divisible by 20.

title: Story: The Bicycle Odometer With Wheel Size Switch
description: You're designing an odometer for a bicycle. The wheel sensor pulses (pulse=1) once per revolution. The wheel radius depends on bike type: road bike (small) = 2 meters circumference, mountain bike (large) = 2.5 meters. A switch (bike_type) selects 0 for small, 1 for large. Distance should accumulate in meters using only integer arithmetic (use 20 and 25 as tenths of meters, divide later). Output total_meters[15:0] the total distance after each revolution. Reset clears the odometer.
hint: Track tenths of meters in a separate register; convert to meters only for the output. Add 20 or 25 depending on bike_type.

title: Story: The Camera Shutter Trigger With Anti-Shake Delay
description: Design the shutter trigger logic for a camera. When the shutter button is pressed (shutter=1 pulse), the camera waits 20 cycles (anti-shake) before firing. If the button is released (shutter_release=1) during that wait, the shot is cancelled. Once fired, the shutter stays open for the configured exposure time (exposure[7:0] cycles), then closes and asserts done=1 for 1 cycle. Reset cancels everything.
template:
module shutter (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire shutter,
    input wire shutter_release,
    input wire [7:0] exposure,
    output reg fire,
    output reg done
);
    // 20-cycle delay, then exposure, then done
endmodule
hint: Three states: WAIT (20 cycles), OPEN (exposure cycles), then back to IDLE with done pulse. shutter_release aborts WAIT.

title: Story: The Cash Register That Computes Change
description: Design the change calculation logic for a cash register. Item price arrives as price[15:0] (in cents). Customer pays amount (paid[15:0]). Compute change = paid - price. Then output how many of each bill/coin to return: 100c, 25c, 10c, 5c, 1c. Output on change_valid=1 pulse. If paid < price, no change and error=1. Reset clears outputs.
template:
module cash_register (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire calc,
    input wire [15:0] price,
    input wire [15:0] paid,
    output reg [15:0] change,
    output reg [7:0] n100,
    output reg [7:0] n25,
    output reg [7:0] n10,
    output reg [7:0] n5,
    output reg [7:0] n1,
    output reg change_valid,
    output reg error
);
    // Greedy change making
endmodule
hint: Greedy change: divide by 100, then remainder by 25, then remainder by 10, then remainder by 5, remainder = n1.

title: Story: The Digital Dice That Rolls on a Button
description: You are designing a digital dice for a board game. Pressing the roll button (roll=1 pulse) starts the dice spinning: the value cycles 1..6 rapidly (every clock). It stops when you release the button — no wait, simpler: it spins for exactly 8 cycles after the press, then stops and shows the final value 1..6. Reset clears to 1. A new press restarts the spin. Output value[2:0] (must always be in 1..6).
hint: Counter for the number of spins left. When roll, load 8; else decrement and roll the dice value 1..6.

title: Story: The Digital Thermometer With Min/Max Tracking
description: A digital thermometer takes a new temperature each clock (temp_valid=1). It tracks the current temperature, the minimum ever seen, and the maximum ever seen. Output current[7:0], min_temp[7:0], max_temp[7:0]. When rst is asserted, min=255 and max=0 (so any real temperature updates them). This is a tracking FSM.
template:
module thermometer (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire temp_valid,
    input wire [7:0] temp,
    output reg [7:0] current,
    output reg [7:0] min_temp,
    output reg [7:0] max_temp
);
    // Track min/max
endmodule
solution:
module thermometer (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire temp_valid,
    input wire [7:0] temp,
    output reg [7:0] current,
    output reg [7:0] min_temp,
    output reg [7:0] max_temp
);
    always @(posedge clk)
        if (rst) begin current<=0; min_temp<=8'hFF; max_temp<=8'h00; end
        else if (temp_valid) begin
            current <= temp;
            if (temp < min_temp) min_temp <= temp;
            if (temp > max_temp) max_temp <= temp;
        end
endmodule
hint: Three registers. Initialize min=255 and max=0 so any input updates them.

title: Story: The Drone Arming Sequence
description: You are writing the arming logic for a drone. To arm the motors, the pilot must hold the arm switch (arm_switch=1) while the throttle stick is fully down (throttle_zero=1) for 100 consecutive cycles. If the stick moves off zero at any point, the count resets. Once armed, motors_enable=1 and stays 1 until either disarm (disarm=1 pulse) or a failsafe condition (failsafe=1) occurs. Arming must not happen within 200 cycles of reset (safety delay). Design the FSM.
template:
module drone_arm (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire arm_switch,
    input wire throttle_zero,
    input wire disarm,
    input wire failsafe,
    output reg motors_enable
);
    // 100-cycle hold, 200-cycle safety delay
endmodule
hint: Two counters: a one-shot safety counter and a hold counter that resets if the pilot lets go. Once armed, only disarm/failsafe clear it.

examples.input: arm + thr_zero for 100 cycles after safety

title: Story: The Electronic Voting Machine
description: A voting machine accepts votes from 4 voters. Each voter has a button: v0, v1, v2, v3. When the chairman presses 'commit' (commit=1 pulse), the machine stores the current total and locks (locked=1). Only one vote per voter (each button press increments a total count, so if a voter presses 3 times it counts 3 — simplified). The total count after commit is output total[7:0]. Pressing reset unlocks and clears. Use a saturating counter so it doesn't overflow past 255.
template:
module voting_machine (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire v0,
    input wire v1,
    input wire v2,
    input wire v3,
    input wire commit,
    output reg [7:0] total,
    output reg locked
);
    // Sum votes; lock on commit
endmodule
solution:
module voting_machine (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire v0,
    input wire v1,
    input wire v2,
    input wire v3,
    input wire commit,
    output reg [7:0] total,
    output reg locked
);
    wire any_vote = v0 | v1 | v2 | v3;
    always @(posedge clk)
        if (rst) begin total<=0; locked<=0; end
        else begin
            if (commit) locked <= 1;
            if (!locked && any_vote && total < 8'd255) total <= total + 8'd1;
        end
endmodule
hint: Combinational OR of votes plus a saturating counter. locked gates the counter.

title: Story: The Fitness Tracker Step Counter
description: You are designing the step counter for a fitness tracker. The accelerometer gives a step_pulse=1 for each step. The device also has a goal: goal_steps is set by the user (16-bit). The output goal_reached=1 permanently once the goal is met (until reset). The device can also enter power-save mode (pwr_save=1) in which step counting is paused and the current count is preserved. Reset clears the counter and the goal_reached flag.
template:
module step_counter (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire step_pulse,
    input wire pwr_save,
    input wire [15:0] goal_steps,
    output reg [15:0] steps,
    output reg goal_reached
);
    // count steps, compare to goal
endmodule
solution:
module step_counter (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire step_pulse,
    input wire pwr_save,
    input wire [15:0] goal_steps,
    output reg [15:0] steps,
    output reg goal_reached
);
    always @(posedge clk)
        if (rst) begin steps<=0; goal_reached<=0; end
        else begin
            if (!goal_reached && step_pulse && !pwr_save) begin
                steps <= steps + 16'd1;
                if (steps + 16'd1 >= goal_steps) goal_reached <= 1;
            end
        end
endmodule
hint: Simple counter + comparator. pwr_save gates increment. goal_reached latches once set.

title: Story: The Guitar Tuner That Detects Notes
description: A simple guitar tuner. A frequency counter produces a frequency value each measurement (freq[15:0]). The tuner compares the frequency to the target for the selected string and outputs whether the string is sharp, flat, or in tune. Strings: E (82 Hz), A (110), D (146), G (196), B (246), E (329). Tolerance ±3 Hz. Combinational logic selects the target based on string select string_sel[2:0] (0-5), and outputs sharp, flat, in_tune.
hint: Case lookup for the target; then three comparisons against target±3.

title: Story: The Kitchen Scale With Tare
description: Design a digital kitchen scale. The load cell sends weight value[15:0] in grams. There is a tare button (tare=1 pulse). When pressed, the current weight becomes the zero point (offset). The displayed weight = raw - offset, saturating at 0. The scale also has a unit switch (unit=0 grams, unit=1 ounces with 1 oz = 28 g). Output displayed[15:0] in the selected unit. Reset clears the tare offset and displayed weight.
hint: Store the offset on tare. Compute grams = max(raw-offset, 0). For ounces, divide by 28 using synthesizable integer division (constant divisor).

title: Story: The Microwave That Runs for N Seconds
description: You are writing the FSM for a microwave. The user presses start (start=1 pulse) and enters a time in seconds (time_in[7:0]). The microwave runs for that many cycles. During operation, if the door opens (door_open=1), it pauses and the magnetron turns off; when the door closes, it resumes from the same second. Pressing stop (stop=1 pulse) aborts the run. When the timer reaches 0, a beep pulses for 3 cycles and the FSM returns to IDLE. Reset clears to IDLE.
template:
module microwave (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire start,
    input wire stop,
    input wire door_open,
    input wire [7:0] time_in,
    output reg magnetron,
    output reg beep
);
    // Countdown with pause on door
endmodule
hint: Track remaining count. Door pauses only the countdown and turns off magnetron. Stop aborts. Beep 3 cycles when cnt hits 0.

title: Story: The Motion-Activated Smart Bulb
description: You're designing a smart bulb controller. It has a motion sensor (motion=1 pulse) and an ambient-light sensor (dark=1 when dark). The bulb turns on when motion is detected AND it is dark. Once on, it stays on for 200 cycles (5 seconds), extending the timer each time motion is detected again. The bulb can be manually turned off with a wall switch (force_off=1 pulse). The bulb cannot be turned on if it's not dark. Reset turns the bulb off.
solution:
module smart_bulb (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire motion,
    input wire dark,
    input wire force_off,
    output reg bulb_on
);
    reg [7:0] timer;
    always @(posedge clk)
        if (rst) begin timer<=0; bulb_on<=0; end
        else if (force_off) begin timer<=0; bulb_on<=0; end
        else if (motion && dark) begin timer<=8'd200; bulb_on<=1; end
        else if (timer > 0) begin timer <= timer - 1; bulb_on <= 1; end
        else bulb_on <= 0;
endmodule
hint: Single timer that reloads on motion when dark. Bulb is on iff timer > 0 (or motion just happened). force_off wins.

title: Story: The Office Parking Gate That Counts Cars
description: You're designing the controller for a parking lot gate. The lot has exactly 8 spots. A sensor detects a car entering (enter=1 pulse) and another detects a car leaving (exit=1 pulse). The gate opens when there is at least one free spot and a car is at the entrance (want_in=1). The gate closes when no car is at the entrance. If the lot is full (8 cars), the gate stays closed and a 'FULL' sign lights up (full=1). Cars can't leave if the lot is empty. Design a controller that tracks occupancy and drives gate_open and full.
template:
module parking_gate (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire enter,
    input wire exit,
    input wire want_in,
    output reg gate_open,
    output reg full
);
    // 8-space lot
endmodule
hint: Just an up/down counter 0..8. full when count==8. gate_open is a combinational AND of want_in and !full.

title: Story: The Smart Lock That Locks Out After 3 Wrong PINs
description: A smart door lock accepts a 4-bit PIN each attempt. The correct PIN is 1010. Each attempt is made by pressing 'submit' (submit=1 pulse). If the PIN matches, unlock=1 pulse and the wrong-counter resets. If the PIN is wrong, increment wrong_counter. After 3 wrong attempts, lockout=1 (permanent) and the lock refuses any PIN (ignores submit) until master_reset=1. Reset clears everything.
template:
module smart_lock (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire master_reset,
    input wire submit,
    input wire [3:0] pin,
    output reg unlock,
    output reg lockout
);
    // 3 wrong attempts -> lockout
endmodule
solution:
module smart_lock (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire master_reset,
    input wire submit,
    input wire [3:0] pin,
    output reg unlock,
    output reg lockout
);
    reg [1:0] wrong;
    always @(posedge clk)
        if (rst) begin wrong<=0; unlock<=0; lockout<=0; end
        else begin
            unlock <= 0;
            if (master_reset) begin wrong<=0; lockout<=0; end
            else if (!lockout && submit) begin
                if (pin == 4'b1010) begin unlock<=1; wrong<=0; end
                else begin
                    wrong <= wrong + 2'd1;
                    if (wrong == 2'd2) lockout <= 1;
                end
            end
        end
endmodule
hint: Wrong counter 0..2. Lockout latches at wrong==2. master_reset clears both. Correct PIN resets the wrong counter.

title: Story: The Smart Thermostat With Hysteresis
description: You're designing a smart thermostat. The user sets a target temperature target[7:0]. The measured temperature temp[7:0] arrives every cycle. The heater (heater_on) turns on when temp < target - 2 and turns off when temp >= target + 1 (hysteresis to avoid rapid toggling). The AC (ac_on) turns on when temp > target + 2 and off when temp <= target - 1. Heater and AC must never be on at the same time. Reset turns both off.
solution:
module thermostat (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire [7:0] temp,
    input wire [7:0] target,
    output reg heater_on,
    output reg ac_on
);
    always @(posedge clk)
        if (rst) begin heater_on<=0; ac_on<=0; end
        else begin
            if (heater_on) begin
                if (temp >= target + 8'd1) heater_on <= 0;
            end else if (ac_on) begin
                if (temp <= target - 8'd1) ac_on <= 0;
            end else begin
                if (temp + 8'd2 < target) heater_on <= 1;
                else if (temp > target + 8'd2) ac_on <= 1;
            end
        end
endmodule
hint: Priority: if heater is on, only check turn-off. Else if AC is on, only check turn-off. Else check turn-on conditions.

title: Story: The Stadium Turnstile With Anti-Passback
description: A stadium turnstile has two sensors: entry_sensor=1 when someone breaks the beam at the entry, exit_sensor=1 at the exit. A valid ticket scan (ticket=1 pulse) allows one entry. After a valid entry, the same ticket cannot be reused until the person exits (exit_sensor). If someone tries to enter without a valid ticket, alarm=1 for one cycle. Design the FSM. Only one person in the turnstile at a time.
template:
module turnstile (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire ticket,
    input wire entry_sensor,
    input wire exit_sensor,
    output reg gate_open,
    output reg alarm
);
    // Anti-passback: entry allowed only after exit
endmodule
hint: Two flags: 'armed' (ticket validated, waiting for entry) and 'inside' (person currently in). Anti-passback: no entry if inside.

title: Story: The Wireless Doorbell With Ring Suppression
description: Design the doorbell logic. A button press (button=1 pulse) should ring the bell (ring=1 pulse). To prevent ringing multiple times for one press, ignore any subsequent press within 500 cycles (debounce/suppression window). If the button is held for more than 3 cycles, treat it as a long press and use a different chime (chime_long=1 instead of chime_short=1). Reset clears the suppression timer.
hint: Track hold length while button is pressed; on release, if suppression is off, ring based on hold length and start suppression.

title: Story: HDLC Bit Stuffer (Combinational + Sequential)
description: High-Level Data Link Control (HDLC) uses bit stuffing: after five consecutive 1s in the data stream, a 0 is inserted. Unlike CAN, HDLC only stuffs on 1s. The DUT receives bits one per clock (in_valid, in_bit), and emits bits on out_valid, out_bit. After 5 consecutive 1s, insert a 0 and reset the count. Data resets the count. This is a combined datapath + control design.
hint: Similar to CAN stuffing but only on 1s. Use a pending flag to emit the 0 on the next cycle.

title: Story: The 3-Floor Elevator That Remembers Requests
description: You're building the FSM for a 3-floor building elevator. Floors are numbered 0 (ground), 1, and 2. There are three call buttons: call0, call1, call2 — each pulses once when pressed. The elevator starts at floor 0. It moves one floor per clock in the direction of the lowest-priority-but-unserved call (up first, then down). When the elevator reaches a called floor, it stops for 1 cycle (doors open, stop=1) and clears that request. The output floor[1:0] shows the current floor; stop pulses one cycle when doors open. Design the request memory and the movement FSM.
template:
module elevator3 (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire call0,
    input wire call1,
    input wire call2,
    output reg [1:0] floor,
    output reg stop
);
    // 3-floor elevator, up-first priority
endmodule
hint: Register the requests (req[2:0]) so a single pulse is remembered. Stop when current floor is requested, else move one step toward the nearest requested floor.

title: Story: The Coffee Machine That Only Accepts Exact Change
description: You're building the controller for a coffee vending machine at a small office. Coffee costs 50 cents. The machine accepts only two coins: a 25-cent coin and a 10-cent coin (two buttons: c25, c10). The machine accumulates coins and dispenses exactly one cup as soon as the accumulated amount reaches or exceeds 50 cents, then pays back the overpayment in 25c and 10c coins, one coin per cycle, with a 1-cycle pulse on change25 / change10. Inserting 25+25 gives an exact 50c and no change; inserting 25+10+10 (45c) followed by another 25c reaches 70c, so the machine dispenses and returns 20c as two 10c coins. Output: dispense (1-cycle pulse), change25, change10. Reset clears the accumulated total.
template:
module coffee_machine (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire coin25,
    input wire coin10,
    output reg dispense,
    output reg change25,
    output reg change10
);
    // Coffee = 50c. Accept 25c / 10c. Give exact change.
endmodule
hint: Two-phase FSM: accept coins until total >= 50, then emit change one coin per cycle. Total and change are small counters (0-99).

title: Story: The Crosswalk Button That Extends Green
description: You're designing a traffic-light controller for a small intersection with a crosswalk. Normal cycle: RED (40 cycles), GREEN (60 cycles), YELLOW (10 cycles), then back to RED. There is a crosswalk button (ped=1 pulse). If the pedestrian presses during RED, the controller shortens the next RED by 20 cycles (to give them a walk sooner — but still safe). If pressed during GREEN or YELLOW, nothing changes immediately, but the next RED runs 20 cycles longer. Outputs red, green, yellow, and walk (walk=1 during the last 10 cycles of RED when a pedestrian has requested). Reset returns to RED with no pedestrian request.
template:
module crosswalk (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire ped,
    output reg red,
    output reg green,
    output reg yellow,
    output reg walk
);
    // RED 40, GREEN 60, YELLOW 10; ped modifies RED
endmodule
hint: Keep a red_len register that is set when ped arrives. walk asserts during the last 10 cycles of RED when ped_seen. Reset red_len to 40 after leaving RED.

title: Story: The Metro Ticket Machine With Limited Coins
description: A metro ticket costs 20 cents. The machine accepts 5c and 10c coins (buttons c5, c10). It has only 3 coins of 5c left in the change dispenser and 2 coins of 10c. If a user overpays and the machine can't return change, it must refund the entire transaction (refund=1 pulse) and NOT issue a ticket. Ticket issued as issue=1 pulse. The machine holds at most one transaction at a time. Reset clears everything and resets the change reserves to 3 (5c) and 2 (10c).
hint: Track reserves for change. When change is needed, deduct from reserves greedily (10c first). If not enough, refund instead of issuing.

title: Story: The Office Printer Job Queue
description: A simple office printer holds up to 4 print jobs in a queue. When a job arrives (new_job=1 pulse), it's enqueued. When the printer is idle (busy=0) and a job is queued, it dequeues one and prints it (busy=1 for 5 cycles, prints=1 during that time). If the queue is full and a new job arrives, a 'reject' pulse is emitted and the job is dropped. Reset clears the queue. Output queue_count[2:0].
template:
module printer_queue (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire new_job,
    output reg busy,
    output reg prints,
    output reg reject,
    output reg [2:0] queue_count
);
    // 4-slot queue, prints for 5 cycles
endmodule
hint: Counter for queue depth + busy timer. Reject when full. Print 5 cycles (timer 4..0).

title: Story: The Smart Bulb That Fades In and Out
description: A smart bulb has a fade feature. When turned on (turn_on=1 pulse), the brightness ramps from 0 to 255 over 256 cycles (1 step/cycle). When turned off (turn_off=1 pulse), brightness ramps from current to 0 over 256 cycles. The output brightness[7:0] is the current value; the bulb_on signal indicates whether the bulb is ramping or steady-on. Reset sets brightness to 0, bulb_on to 0.
hint: Direction flag and a simple increment/decrement. bulb_on follows the direction (1 while ramping up or held at 255).

title: Story: The Smart Pill Dispenser
description: Design a pill dispenser controller. The user sets the number of pills per day (pills_per_day[3:0], 1-15) and presses start. The device dispenses one pill every 24 hours (model 1 hour = 1000 cycles). After dispensing each pill, it waits for the user to take it (taken=1 pulse within 100 cycles) before continuing. If not taken, alarm=1 pulse and the device waits indefinitely until taken. After the last pill of the day, the device goes to SLEEP for 24 hours minus the time already spent. Reset clears everything.
template:
module pill_dispenser (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire start,
    input wire taken,
    input wire [3:0] pills_per_day,
    output reg dispense,
    output reg alarm,
    output reg asleep
);
    // 1 hour = 1000 cycles
endmodule
hint: Multiple states: idle, wait 1 hour, dispense, wait for taken (100-cycle timeout alarm), sleep 24h. Track pills_left.

title: Story: The Vending Machine That Gives Change First
description: A vending machine has a coin return feature. When the user inserts coins (5c, 10c, 25c) but then presses the coin return button (return_btn=1 pulse), the machine must return the exact same coins in the same order they were inserted. Design a stack (LIFO) so the last coin inserted is the first returned. Output coins one per cycle with a coin_valid pulse; each return_coin[1:0] encodes 0=5c, 1=10c, 2=25c. Reset clears the stack.
template:
module coin_return (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire insert5,
    input wire insert10,
    input wire insert25,
    input wire return_btn,
    output reg [1:0] return_coin,
    output reg coin_valid
);
    // Stack-based coin return
endmodule
hint: Use a stack (array + stack pointer). Push on insert, pop on return. Return the popped value with a valid pulse.

title: Story: The Washing Machine Cycle Controller
description: You are writing the FSM for a residential washing machine. The user presses start (start=1 pulse). The machine goes through: FILL (30 cycles), WASH (50 cycles), DRAIN (20 cycles), RINSE (30 cycles), SPIN (40 cycles), DONE (1 cycle pulse), back to IDLE. During any phase, if the lid opens (lid_open=1), the machine pauses (state holds) until the lid closes. The motor (motor_on) is only on during WASH and SPIN. The water valve (valve_open) is only open during FILL and RINSE. The drain pump (drain_on) is only on during DRAIN. Output a busy flag that is 1 whenever not in IDLE. Reset returns to IDLE.
template:
module washer (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire start,
    input wire lid_open,
    output reg motor_on,
    output reg valve_open,
    output reg drain_on,
    output reg busy,
    output reg done
);
    // FILL 30 -> WASH 50 -> DRAIN 20 -> RINSE 30 -> SPIN 40 -> DONE
endmodule
